title: Lattice composite Fermi liquid with broken inversion symmetry
authors: Pavel A. Nosov, Zhengyan Darius Shi
abstract: We study transport in lattice composite Fermi liquids realized in half-filled Chern bands with broken inversion symmetry. We show that reduced crystalline symmetry exposes intrinsic singular dynamical responses of composite fermions that are otherwise hidden in the conventional Landau-level setting. At zero wave vector, inversion breaking allows gauge-field fluctuations to generate a non-analytic longitudinal optical resistivity, with $\operatorname{Re}ρ^{xx}(ω)\sim |ω|^{4/3}$ for gate-screened Coulomb interactions. At finite wave vector $\mathbf{q}$, inversion breaking leads to nonreciprocal transport and a non-analytic $\sim |\mathbf{q}|$ dependence of the Hall conductivity, both of which can be probed through surface acoustic wave propagation. We also discuss a distinct mechanism for singular DC transport in lattice composite Fermi liquids: renormalization of $2k_F$ scattering at the composite Fermi surface enhances Umklapp relaxation and can lead to a non-analytic temperature dependence of the resistivity. Taken together, our results identify transport signatures of lattice composite Fermi liquids that are absent in their continuum quantum Hall counterparts and can be directly tested in ongoing experiments on twisted MoTe$_2$ and rhombohedral graphene, where evidence for zero-field composite Fermi liquids has recently been reported.
summary: This theoretical work investigates transport phenomena in lattice composite Fermi liquids where inversion symmetry is broken. The authors derive unique, non-analytic scaling laws for optical resistivity and Hall conductivity that are forbidden in simpler continuum models. These predictions offer testable signatures for experimental measurements on advanced 2D materials.
main_problem: To determine the distinct transport signatures of lattice composite Fermi liquids (CFLs) when inversion symmetry is broken, comparing them to continuum quantum Hall systems.
main_result: Inversion breaking leads to non-analytic longitudinal optical resistivity ($\sim |\omega|^{4/3}$ at $q=0$) and nonreciprocal transport ($\sim |q|$ dependence in $\sigma_{LT}$) that are absent in symmetric CFLs.
method: Analytical calculations using effective field theory, parton decomposition, and scaling analysis of quantum corrections to conductivity tensors.
model_or_system: Lattice composite Fermi liquids realized in half-filled Chern bands with broken inversion symmetry. The system is modeled via an effective action involving composite fermions (CFs) interacting with gauge fields.
key_observables: Longitudinal optical resistivity ($	ext{Re } ho_{xx}(\omega)$), Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{LT}$), and DC resistivity temperature dependence ($	ext{Re } ho_{xx}(T)$).
important_parameters: Zero wave vector ($q=0$), finite wave vector ($q$), frequency ($\omega$), and temperature ($T$). The symmetry breaking parameter $\lambda$ is crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the kinematic regime for surface acoustic wave probes and uses approximations like Random Phase Approximation (RPA) in some derivations.
figures_summary: Not specified, but notes reference specific equations (e.g., B25-B28) detailing scaling of correlation functions involving diamagnetic and paramagnetic vertices.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes transport properties by first establishing the effective theory for CFLs, then calculating response functions ($\Pi$) using diagrammatic techniques, focusing on how symmetry breaking modifies the low-energy scaling exponents for resistivity and conductivity components.
why_interesting: It provides concrete, measurable signatures (non-analytic power laws in $\omega$ or $q$) that distinguish lattice models from continuum theories, offering direct guidance for interpreting THz/acoustic measurements in novel 2D materials like twisted MoTe2.
